issues.failure_explanation: The formulation contains no boundary-condition mechanism. The boundary-face part of $R_\theta(D_k)$ is computed entirely from the network's own trace $U_\theta$, and no prescribed boundary data appears in $R_\theta$, $L_{\mathrm{cons}}$, $L_{\mathrm{ent}}$, or among the inputs of Algorithm 1. Evaluating a flux with unconstrained network values enforces nothing; for an inflow boundary the exact solution depends on boundary data the loss never sees, so the asserted enforcement is false for any nontrivial boundary condition.

failure_location.quote: When a boundary face of a control volume $D_k$ coincides with the physical boundary of the domain $\Omega_x$, the flux integration across this face directly enforces the prescribed boundary conditions naturally through the evaluation of $R_\theta(D_k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or weaken the sentence, and either add an explicit boundary-data term to the loss or restrict the stated scope to problems whose waves do not interact with the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed boundary-condition capability of WE-PINNs is unfounded. No formal result or reported experiment depends on it (the test waves never reach the boundary), so the loss is confined to this claim.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that boundary-face flux evaluation enforces boundary conditions
issues.why_classification: A local edit (removing the unsupported claim, or adding a standard boundary penalty) resolves it; no theorem, guarantee, or reported result depends on boundary-condition enforcement.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's central step is a non sequitur. $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}$ is built from the Kruzhkov fluxes $|U_\theta-k|$ and $\mathrm{sgn}(U_\theta-k)(F(U_\theta)-F(k))$, which are neither the conserved fluxes $(U_\theta,F(U_\theta))$ defining $R_\theta(D_i)$ nor the fixed entropy pair $(\eta,q)$ defining $E_\theta(D_i)$, so no divergence-theorem manipulation yields the claimed decomposition; the object $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i,k)$ is never defined. If one integrates by parts on each $D_i$, the boundary terms contain $\varphi$ itself, whose $L^\infty$ norm is unbounded over $\mathcal{A}$ (only derivatives of $\varphi$ are bounded), so 'factoring out the derivatives of $\varphi$' cannot be performed. Independent additional defects: (i) the $1/N_D$ prefactor in the loss definitions contradicts the Cauchy--Schwarz step, which carries an extra factor $\sqrt{N_D}$; (ii) the supremum over all $k\in\mathbb{R}$ (the full Kruzhkov family) is claimed to be controlled by the single entropy pair in $L_{\mathrm{ent}}$, with no argument; (iii) the lemma assumes a fixed partition while the losses are computed on dynamically sampled, generally overlapping volumes. The statement is also false in the shock regime: the entropy solution of a Riemann problem has zero conservation loss and zero one-sided entropy loss but strictly positive $E_R$ (dissipation across the shock), and smooth approximations of it have vanishing losses with $E_R$ bounded away from zero, contradicting the asserted bound.

failure_location.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals, corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the non sequitur by a genuine argument controlling a violation-direction Kruzhkov truncation error (supremum over all $k$) by the actual boundary-flux losses, consistently treating the $1/N_D$ normalization, the sampled non-partition volumes, and bounded test functions, or redesign the entropy loss accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The central linkage between the training losses and the continuous truncation error is unestablished and false as stated, so Step 3 of the main convergence theorem (thm:added-2) has no valid input, and the abstract's claim of a rigorous loss-to-$L^1$-error analysis is unsupported.
issues.title: Link lemma between discrete losses and Kruzhkov truncation error is unproven and false
issues.why_classification: The lemma is false as stated and its proof fails at the central step; no source-supported resolution exists, since controlling the Kruzhkov family with the paper's single-entropy boundary-flux losses requires essentially new analysis (and plausibly a redesigned loss), and the paper's central convergence claim fails without it.

\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(U_\theta) = \int_0^T \int_\Omega \left( |U_\theta - k|\partial_t \varphi + \text{sgn}(U_\theta - k)(F(U_\theta) - F(k))\cdot \nabla_x \varphi \right) dx\, dt.
\partial_t \eta(U) + \nabla_x \cdot q(U) \le 0

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's definitions $E_R$ is not a truncation error: testing the Kruzhkov admissibility inequality (cf. the paper's own $\partial_t\eta+\nabla_x\cdot q\le 0$) against $\varphi\ge 0$ gives $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(u)\ge 0$ for entropy solutions, strictly positive across shocks, so $\sup\mathcal{R}$ measures entropy dissipation and is zero for entropy-violating solutions. Counterexample: inviscid Burgers with $u_0=0$ for $x\le -0.25$ and $1$ otherwise; let $u$ be the rarefaction and $v$ the expansion shock $v=0$ for $x<-0.25+t/2$, $v=1$ otherwise (a bounded weak solution with $v(\cdot,0)=u_0$ and $\sup_t TV(v(\cdot,t))=1$). For $k\notin[0,1]$ the defect measure vanishes, so $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(v)=0$; for $k\in(0,1)$ it equals $k(1-k)\,\delta_{x=-0.25+t/2}>0$, so $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(v)\le 0$ for all $\varphi\ge 0$. Hence $E_R(v)=0$ and the initial error is $0$, yet $\|v(\cdot,T)-u(\cdot,T)\|_{L^1}>0$; the stated estimate bounds a positive number by $0$ and is false. The failure lies in the statement itself (no proof is reproduced), so it is neither a failed inference within a proof, an unestablished premise of a proof, nor a support mismatch; the root is the wrong-sign definition of $E_R$ embedded in the statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The analysis operates on a spatial domain of finite measure (Lemma 1's constant $\sqrt{|\Omega\times(0,T)|}$; experiments on $[-1,1]$ and $[0,1]$) but no boundary condition is ever specified, enforced, or hypothesized. On a bounded domain without boundary data the posited unique entropy solution need not exist: for Burgers on $[-1,1]$ with $u_0\equiv 1$, both $u\equiv 1$ and the solution with a compressive wave entering from $x=-1$ ($v=2$ for $x<-1+\tfrac32 t$, $v=1$ otherwise) satisfy the same initial data and all Kruzhkov entropy inequalities in the interior. The invoked Kruzhkov/Bouchut-Perthame theory concerns the Cauchy problem on $\mathbb{R}^d$ or requires boundary hypotheses, so its use here is outside its hypotheses; moreover the losses are blind to inflow data (any weak solution has zero conservation residuals, and entropy-admissible ones also zero one-sided entropy residual), so convergence to 'the' entropy solution cannot hold in this setting.

failure_location.quote: Consequently, as $L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta) \to 0$ and $L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta) \to 0$ simultaneously, $U_\theta$ converges to the unique physically admissible entropy solution $u$ in $L^1(\Omega)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing hypotheses: either pose the convergence analysis as a Cauchy problem on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (adjusting the finite-measure constants), or specify boundary conditions and include the boundary treatment required by the Kruzhkov/Bouchut-Perthame theory on bounded domains.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee does not apply to the bounded-domain setting in which the method is used whenever boundary interaction or inflow is present; the hypotheses of thm:added-1 and thm:added-2 are ill-posed there. The reported tests (waves away from the boundary) are not affected.
issues.title: Convergence theorems posed on bounded domains with no boundary conditions; 'unique entropy solution' ill-posed
issues.why_classification: Adding standard hypotheses (whole-space Cauchy problem, or explicit boundary conditions) yields a well-posed, recognizably comparable convergence statement without new proof architecture, and the reported experiments are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: C \sqrt{TV(u_0) \cdot \sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(v(\cdot, t)) \cdot \sqrt{E_R(v)}}
E_R(U_\theta) \leq \sqrt{|\Omega \times (0,T)|} \cdot \left( \sqrt{L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)} + \sqrt{L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)} \right).
\|U_\theta(\cdot, T) - u(\cdot, T)\|_{L^1(\Omega)} \leq K_{\mathrm{opt}} \cdot \left(L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)^{1/4} + L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)^{1/4}\right).

issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 1 the second term equals $C\,(TV(u_0)\sup_t TV(v))^{1/2}E_R(v)^{1/4}$: the outer square root also applies to $\sqrt{E_R}$. Substituting Lemma 1's bound $E_R\le b$, with $b=|\Omega\times(0,T)|^{1/2}(\sqrt{L_{\mathrm{cons}}}+\sqrt{L_{\mathrm{ent}}})$, therefore yields $C(TV(u_0)M)^{1/2}b^{1/4}$, i.e. a rate of order $L^{1/8}$. Step 4 instead asserts the bound with $b^{1/2}$, in effect applying the Lemma-1 bound to $\sqrt{E_R}$ rather than to $E_R$ and claiming a strictly stronger estimate than the cited theorem provides (for small losses $b^{1/2}\ll b^{1/4}$). The stated rate $K_{\mathrm{opt}}(L_{\mathrm{cons}}^{1/4}+L_{\mathrm{ent}}^{1/4})$ therefore does not follow from the stated ingredients, which support only the exponent $1/8$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct Step 4 by applying the nested radical of Theorem 1 as stated and restate Theorem 2 with the supported rate $K(L_{\mathrm{cons}}^{1/8}+L_{\mathrm{ent}}^{1/8})$, adjusting the optimality remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence rate of the main theorem, and the remark declaring 1/4 optimal and 1/2 attainable on structured grids, are not established; the correct rate from the given ingredients is $L^{1/8}$.
issues.title: Step 4 of the convergence proof drops a square root; the claimed 1/4 rate is unsupported
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the algebra restores a valid derivation at the cost of a weakened exponent (1/8 instead of 1/4); the convergence guarantee and its structure survive, so the loss is limited.

This construction guarantees $U_\theta(x,0) \equiv U_0(x)$, eliminating the initial condition error term from the convergence analysis.
The TVD regularization guarantees $\sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(U_\theta(\cdot, t)) \leq M$ for some constant $M$;

issues.failure_explanation: First, a penalty term added to a training loss cannot guarantee the uniform bound $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}TV(U_\theta(\cdot,t))\le M$; nothing in the source establishes any TV bound for trained networks, yet Section 3.4, hypothesis 2 and Step 2 of Theorem 2 present the bound as ensured by the TVD term. Second, the construction is structurally self-defeating: the temporal ansatz forces $U_\theta(\cdot,0)\equiv u_0$, hence $L_{\mathrm{TVD}}(\theta)\ge TV(u_0)>0$ for every $\theta$ whenever $u_0$ is non-constant ($TV(u_0)=1$ in all Riemann tests); with weight $\lambda_{\mathrm{TVD}}=1$ the total loss is bounded below by $TV(u_0)$, can never approach zero, and its minimization rewards suppressing the variation carried by the exact solution (over-smoothing shocks), in direct conflict with the method's purpose and with the convergence narrative that requires $L_{\mathrm{cons}},L_{\mathrm{ent}}\to 0$. Third, the stochastic estimate of $L_{\mathrm{TVD}}$ sums increments over randomly drawn, unsorted points and is not a consistent total-variation estimate as written.

failure_location.quote: To guarantee this condition, we introduce a TVD regularization term:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the TVD penalty by a mechanism that can deliver the bound (e.g., a hinge penalty $\max(0,\sup_t TV-M)^2$ or a projection/constraint), or drop the term and state the TV bound as an explicit assumption; correspondingly weaken the 'guarantee' language and sort the sampled points in the stochastic TV estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The training objective is decoupled from the convergence theory: hypothesis 2 of thm:added-2 is not secured by the TVD term, the claim that minimizing $L(\theta)$ simultaneously enforces flux balance, entropy admissibility and bounded variation is not achieved by the stated loss, and the loss cannot be driven to zero for non-constant data.
issues.title: TVD regularization cannot guarantee the TV bound and makes the total loss non-vanishing
issues.why_classification: A contained construction change (hinge penalty or explicit assumption) plus adjusted wording restores a coherent, comparable method and theory, without new global proof architecture or major scope loss.

issues.failure_explanation: By the temporal ansatz, $U_\theta(\cdot,0)\equiv u_0$ exactly, so every relative error of WE-PINNs at $t=0$ must vanish (Theorem 2, Step 1, uses precisely this). The tables nonetheless report nonzero entries in the $t=0.0$ columns: for the Burgers Riemann problem $E_{L^1}=8.07\times10^{-3}$, $E_{L^2}=5.79\times10^{-2}$, $E_{L^\infty}=7.95\times10^{-1}$, and similarly in the rarefaction, rarefaction-shock, and shallow-water tables. These values are impossible for the method as described: either the experiments did not use the stated ansatz (so the zero-initial-error premise of the convergence analysis does not describe the reported computations) or the $t=0$ data are wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reconcile description and data: correct the $t=0$ entries of the affected tables, or disclose the actual initial-condition handling (e.g., smoothed data or a soft penalty) and adjust the method description and the zero-initial-error narrative accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The credibility of the reported numerical validation is compromised at $t=0$ in four tables, and the exact-initial-condition construction claim is contradicted by the paper's own data; the affected experimental claims require correction or re-verification.
issues.title: Reported t=0 errors are impossible under the exactly imposed initial condition
issues.why_classification: The contradiction cannot be resolved by a single forced correction (the source does not determine which side is wrong); reconciling requires correcting data or the method description and re-validating the affected experimental claims, although the framework and remaining results survive.
